script: A man once died from a single touch of an umbrella tip on a London bridge, and his killer was never found. In September 1978, Bulgarian writer Georgi Markov was waiting for a bus on Waterloo Bridge when he felt a sharp sting in his leg, like an insect bite. A stranger behind him picked up a dropped umbrella and muttered an apology. Markov thought nothing of it, until he developed a high fever that night. Four days later, he was dead. An autopsy found a tiny pellet lodged in his leg, smaller than a pinhead, drilled with microscopic holes and coated in a poison called ricin. The umbrella had fired it into him like a silent gun. Investigators traced the weapon to the Bulgarian secret police, working with the KGB, but the assassin was never officially identified, and the key documents were destroyed. A man once died from a single touch of an umbrella tip, and 45 years later, his killer is still walking free.

title: He Was Killed With a Single Touch of an Umbrella. His Killer Was Never Found
description:
In 1978, Bulgarian dissident Georgi Markov was assassinated on a London bridge with a poison pellet fired from an umbrella. The KGB and Bulgarian secret police were blamed. Nobody was ever charged.

Would you have felt safe in London after this, or been terrified of every stranger with an umbrella?
